customManagers.description: Tool pins in the Forgejo workflows: a `# renovate: datasource=<ds> depName=<name>` comment on the line above a `<NAME>_VERSION: "x.y.z"` env entry (ci.yml's CARGO_AUDIT_VERSION). No built-in manager reads these comments, so without this the pin never gets a PR.

packageRules.description: Group all GitHub Actions bumps into one PR.

Cargo.toml declares loose requirements on purpose (`tauri = "2"`, `cpal = "0.18"`). The global `bump` strategy would rewrite each of those to an exact minor on every release, churning the manifest for no gain. `update-lockfile` instead moves Cargo.lock for in-range updates and only edits Cargo.toml when the new version falls outside the existing requirement. ci.yml builds, lints and tests with `--locked` (`cargo clippy --locked -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo audit` on the lockfile), so the refreshed lock is exactly what gets verified.

Cargo treats a bump of the leftmost non-zero component as breaking: cpal 0.15 -> 0.16 or windows-sys 0.60 -> 0.61 is a semver-MAJOR change. Renovate's cargo versioning is plain semver 2.0, so it labels these updateType `minor` and the major rule at the bottom never sees them. Open the PR and let CI compile both targets, but never automerge: several of these crates are ABI-coupled to something outside their own version (windows-sys must stay on the version Tauri already resolves, or the binary carries two copies; gtk is ignored outright for the same reason). Matched by datasource, not manager, so the cargo-audit pin in the workflows (read by the custom regex manager) gets a human for a 0.x minor too.

Tauri's Rust crates and its JS packages are released in lockstep, and a mismatch between them surfaces as an IPC/type error at runtime rather than a compile error - so they must land in a single PR. This is the one grouping Dependabot structurally cannot express, since its groups never span two ecosystems. Not automerged: ci.yml compiles, lints and unit-tests both halves (`pnpm build` + `pnpm test`, cargo clippy + `cargo test`) but never launches the app, so a regression in the tray-icon / global-shortcut / autostart plugins or at the IPC boundary would pass green.

The text-injection stack: clipboard (arboard), synthetic typing (enigo), XDG RemoteDesktop portal (ashpd). These sit on the paths the clipboard-restore and modifier-release fixes hardened, and ci.yml never injects a keystroke - so even a patch release here can change behaviour invisibly to a green build. Always gets a human.

atspi re-exports atspi-connection's types; the two versions must be compatible or the a11y-bus listener fails to build. Their feature flags are hand-tuned at the declaration site (p2p is deliberately off) - re-read that comment before merging.
wayland-protocols-misc is built against a specific wayland-client; bump them together.

cpal and the pure-Rust `pulseaudio` protocol client: cpal's PulseAudio host is built on that crate and the app also lists microphones through it directly (src-tauri/src/audio), so a lone bump of either links two copies of the client. cpal is also the whole audio path (capture, mic test, cues); ci.yml never opens a device, so it always gets a human.

Hold keyring on 3. The v4 'v1' compat layer broke API-key reads inside the running app on KDE (streaming connects went out unauthenticated -> 403; shipped broken as v0.1.10, reverted in v0.1.11) while a standalone test binary read the same wallet entries fine -- an async-environment interaction between keyring 4's zbus-based store and the app's tokio-reactor zbus (atspi). Lift only after reproducing keys::get() under a running tokio runtime + spawn_blocking and verifying a real dictation round-trip on Plasma.

Hold rubato on the 0.x line. 3.0 is a full API rewrite -- SincFixedIn is gone, replaced by an `Async` resampler driven through buffer adapters (SequentialSliceOfVecs) and an `Indexing` struct -- and it would mean rewriting the live mic->16kHz resampling path for no capability this app needs (simple fixed-input mono sinc). 0.16 serves that with zero code change. Drop this rule and port audio/resample.rs if a 3.x feature is ever actually required.
react and react-dom must ship the identical version, and their @types track the same major.
@tailwindcss/vite is versioned in lockstep with the tailwindcss v4 core.

@vitejs/plugin-react major-peer-depends on a matching vite major (v6 requires vite ^8 and imports vite's `./internal` subpath, which vite 7 does not export). A lone bump of either strands the other on an incompatible peer, so neither PR can ever go green alone -- they must bump as a pair.
The three variable fonts release together - one PR instead of three.
Major bumps require manual review - surface as checkboxes on the Dependency Dashboard, do not open the PR automatically, do not automerge. Minor/patch still flow through automerge gated by ci.
